title: Mission: package the API and explain every Dockerfile line
subtitle: The lunchbox is headed for Kubernetes: light, quick to rebuild, no root and no database password taped to the lid
mission: The intern packaged api-pedidos with the simplest Dockerfile they could find: FROM node:latest, COPY . . before npm ci, the database password in an ENV, no .dockerignore, no USER and the image pushed as latest. It works on their machine (of course). Fix the packaging until all five criteria turn green, and use the table to explain what each line of the final Dockerfile does and why.

coach.ui: Move the controls; the criteria and the Dockerfile change as you adjust. Each failing criterion says why.
coach.cmd: Edit the command and run it. Each failing criterion says why. Everything you need showed up in lessons 2, 3 and 4.

why.simples:
You built the lunchbox the right way: a lean base with a pinned version (no “whatever’s newest”), the beans cooked before the seasoning (dependencies before code, so the cache works), a .dockerignore that keeps junk and .env out, a regular user instead of the owner of the house, and the password handed over at serving time, not taped to the lid.
Notice the domino effect: removing the password from ENV isn’t enough if .env sneaks in with COPY . .; and the slim base only stays light if your machine’s node_modules doesn’t hitch a ride.
why.dev:
Line by line: FROM node:24-slim pins the major version and brings only what’s needed to run Node; ENV NODE_ENV=production turns on libraries’ production mode; WORKDIR /app sets the folder; COPY of the dependency files and RUN npm ci --omit=dev install only what runs in production, in a layer that stays cached; COPY . . brings the code last; USER node switches to the regular user (uid 1000) the official image already ships; EXPOSE 3000 documents the port; CMD in JSON runs node directly.
In the distroless version, the multi-stage build installs dependencies in a stage with tools and copies only /app into a final image with no shell or package manager; the :nonroot tag already runs as a regular user, and the image’s ENTRYPOINT is node, which is why CMD is just ["server.js"]. Secrets go in at run time: docker run -e, a Kubernetes Secret or a vault like Key Vault. For build-time secrets (a private npm token), use RUN --mount=type=secret.
why.especialista:
For production, also: pin the base by digest (FROM node:24-slim@sha256:…) with an update bot; run docker build --check in CI (it warns, for example, about secrets in ARG and ENV and about CMD outside JSON form); generate an SBOM and scan the image; push with an immutable tag and deploy by digest.
In Kubernetes, round it off with securityContext (runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false), requests and limits, and liveness and readiness probes instead of HEALTHCHECK. And mind the signals: Node as PID 1 doesn’t handle SIGTERM by itself, so handle the signal in code (closing the server gracefully) or run with an init (docker run --init; in Kubernetes, handle it in the app), so a rolling update doesn’t cut requests mid-way.

success: Mission accomplished! {text}:{tagStr} is {imgMB} MB, rebuilds in {rebuildS} s when the code changes, runs without root and carries no secrets. And now you can explain every line of the Dockerfile. The lunchbox is ready for Kubernetes.

steps:
Write the fixed Dockerfile and, above each line, a comment (# …) saying why it’s there. That’s the "explain every line" part of the mission:
FROM node:24-slim
ENV NODE_ENV=production
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

Optional, the distroless multi-stage version (in a Dockerfile.distroless file, built with -f Dockerfile.distroless):
FROM node:24-slim AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .

FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs24-debian13:nonroot
ENV NODE_ENV=production
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app /app
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["server.js"]

Check, build and run, passing the password only at run time:
docker build --check .
docker build -t api-pedidos:1.0.0 .
docker run -d --name api -p 3000:3000 -e DB_PASSWORD=change-me api-pedidos:1.0.0
curl http://localhost:3000

Check what is and isn’t in the image:
docker exec api whoami
docker exec api ls -a
docker image inspect api-pedidos:1.0.0 --format "{{.Config.Env}}"
docker image ls api-pedidos
The distroless version has no shell or whoami; use docker image inspect with --format "{{.Config.User}}". At the end: docker rm -f api
recipe.ok: docker build --check finishes with no warnings; curl answers with "Password received: true"; whoami answers node; ls -a shows no .env or .git; and inspect lists NODE_ENV=production but no DB_PASSWORD.
